name: Neck
summary: The rope-like muscles on the sides of your neck that turn and tilt the head and help stabilise it under load.
functions: Rotate the head to the opposite side
Assist breathing by lifting the ribcage
tips: Train the neck gently and progressively — light resistance and slow reps go a long way.
Long hours looking at screens shorten the front of the neck; chin tucks help counter it.

strength.name: Chin Tucks
cues: Sit or stand tall
Glide your chin straight back, making a double chin
Keep your eyes level — don't nod

strength.name: Manual-Resistance Neck Flexion
cues: Place your palm on your forehead
Push your head forward into your hand at ~50% effort
Repeat to each side and the back

strength.name: Lying Neck Curls
cues: Lie on a bench with your head off the end
Hold a light plate on a folded towel on your forehead
Curl chin to chest slowly, lower under control

strength.name: Neck Bridge (Wall)
cues: Stand side-on to a wall with a folded towel between your head and the wall
Lean gently into the towel and hold
Keep the neck long and neutral; build up the lean slowly

strength.name: Band Neck Extension
cues: Loop a light band around the back of your head, anchored in front
Tuck the chin slightly, then extend the head back against the band
Move slowly through a small, pain-free range

flexibility.name: Lateral Neck Stretch
cues: Drop your ear toward your shoulder
Reach the opposite hand toward the floor
Breathe slowly; don't pull hard on the head

flexibility.name: Neck Rotations
cues: Turn to look over one shoulder
Pause, then turn to the other side
Keep the shoulders relaxed and still

flexibility.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
cues: Turn your head 45° and look down toward your armpit
Gently assist with the hand on the back of your head
Keep the opposite shoulder down

flexibility.name: Chin Tuck with Overpressure
cues: Make a double chin
Add gentle pressure on the chin with two fingers
Feel the stretch at the base of the skull

name: Trapezius
summary: A large diamond-shaped muscle from the base of the skull to the mid-back that moves and stabilises the shoulder blades.
functions: Pull the shoulder blades together (middle fibres)
Draw the shoulder blades down and rotate them upward for overhead reaching (lower fibres)
tips: Most people overwork the upper traps and neglect the lower fibres — balance shrugs with Y-raises and face pulls.
Tight upper traps often show up as neck and shoulder tension.

strength.name: Barbell Shrugs
cues: Hold the bar at arm's length
Lift shoulders straight up toward your ears
Pause one second at the top; no rolling

strength.name: Face Pulls
cues: Rope at upper-chest height
Pull toward your face, elbows high and wide
Finish with thumbs pointing behind you

strength.name: Prone Y-Raises
cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench
Raise light dumbbells into a Y shape, thumbs up
Lead with the shoulder blades moving down and back

strength.name: Farmer's Carry
cues: Hold heavy weights at your sides
Stand tall with shoulders packed down
Walk with short, controlled steps

strength.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
cues: Dumbbells at your sides, palms in
Shrug straight up and hold one second
Lower all the way down

strength.name: Rack Pulls
cues: Bar set just below the knees in a rack
Brace and pull to lockout
Squeeze the shoulder blades back at the top

flexibility.name: Upper Trap Stretch
cues: Sit on one hand to anchor that shoulder
Tilt your head away and slightly forward
Gently assist with the other hand

flexibility.name: Shoulder Rolls
cues: Make big slow circles with the shoulders
Squeeze the blades together at the back of each circle

flexibility.name: Thread the Needle (Traps)
cues: On all fours, reach one arm under your body
Let the shoulder and side of the head rest down
Breathe into the upper back

name: Shoulders
summary: The rounded cap of the shoulder with three heads that lift the arm forward, out to the side and back.
functions: Raise the arm out to the side (side head)
tips: Pressing hits the front delts a lot already — give side and rear delts their own work.
Warm up the rotator cuff before heavy overhead pressing.

strength.name: Overhead Press
cues: Bar on the front of the shoulders, grip just outside them
Brace the core and squeeze the glutes
Press straight up, moving your head back then through

strength.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
cues: Slight bend in the elbows
Raise out to the sides to shoulder height
Lead with the elbows; lower slowly

strength.name: Reverse Pec Deck
cues: Chest against the pad, arms straight ahead
Sweep the arms back in a wide arc
Don't shrug — keep the neck long

strength.name: Pike Push-ups
cues: Hips high in an inverted V
Lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands
Press back up through the shoulders

strength.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
cues: Back supported, dumbbells at ear height
Press up until the arms are straight
Lower under control to ear level

strength.name: Arnold Press
cues: Start with palms facing you at chin height
Rotate the palms forward as you press up
Reverse the rotation on the way down

strength.name: Cable Lateral Raise
cues: Stand side-on, handle in the far hand
Raise the arm out to shoulder height
Keep tension on the cable at the bottom

flexibility.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
cues: Bring one arm across your chest
Hug it in with the other forearm above the elbow
Keep the stretched shoulder down

flexibility.name: Band Pull-Aparts
cues: Hold a light band at shoulder height
Pull it apart until it touches your chest
Control the return

flexibility.name: Arm Circles
cues: Arms straight out to the sides
Start with small circles and make them bigger

flexibility.name: Sleeper Stretch
cues: Lie on your side, bottom arm out at 90°
Gently push the forearm toward the floor
Stop at a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder

name: Chest
summary: The fan-shaped muscles across the front of the ribcage that push the arms forward and bring them across the body.
functions: Bring the arms across the body
tips: Vary the bench angle: incline biases the upper chest, flat and decline hit the middle and lower fibres.
A tight chest pulls the shoulders forward — pair chest work with upper-back work.

strength.name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Shoulder blades squeezed back and down
Lower the bar to mid-chest, elbows ~45°
Drive your feet into the floor as you press

strength.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Bench at 30–45°
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest
Press up and slightly in

strength.name: Push-ups
cues: Hands just wider than shoulders
Body in one straight line
Chest touches the floor; elbows tuck slightly

strength.name: Cable Fly
cues: Step forward with a slight lean
Soft bend in the elbows throughout
Hug the handles together in front of your chest

strength.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Dumbbells over the chest, shoulder blades pinched
Lower to the sides of the chest
Press up and slightly together

strength.name: Chest Dips
cues: Lean the torso forward on parallel bars
Lower until the shoulders are just below the elbows
Press back up without shrugging

flexibility.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
cues: Forearm on the doorframe, elbow at shoulder height
Step through gently until you feel the chest open
Keep your ribs down

flexibility.name: Arm Swings
cues: Swing the arms open wide, then cross them in front
Gradually increase the range

flexibility.name: Floor Angels
cues: Lie on your back, arms in a goalpost position
Slide them overhead and back down along the floor
Keep the lower back gently flat

flexibility.name: Foam Roller Chest Opener
cues: Lie lengthways on a foam roller along your spine
Let the arms fall open to the sides, palms up
Breathe slowly and relax into it

name: Biceps
summary: The muscles at the front of the upper arm that bend the elbow and turn the palm up.
tips: Rows and pull-ups train the biceps too — direct curls add the finishing work.
Hammer curls hit the brachialis and forearms, which adds arm thickness.

strength.name: Barbell Curl
cues: Elbows pinned to your sides
Curl without swinging the torso
Lower slowly over 2–3 seconds

strength.name: Hammer Curl
cues: Palms face each other throughout
Curl to the shoulder
Keep your wrists neutral

strength.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
cues: Lie back on a 45–60° bench, arms hanging
Curl without letting the elbows drift forward
Get a full stretch at the bottom

strength.name: Chin-ups
cues: Palms facing you, shoulder-width grip
Pull your chest toward the bar
Lower all the way to straight arms

strength.name: Preacher Curl
cues: Upper arms flat on the pad
Curl up without lifting the elbows
Lower slowly to almost straight

strength.name: Cable Curl
cues: Low pulley, straight bar or rope
Elbows fixed at your sides
Squeeze at the top for one second

flexibility.name: Wall Biceps Stretch
cues: Palm flat on a wall behind you at shoulder height, thumb up
Slowly turn your body away from the wall
Keep the elbow straight but not locked

flexibility.name: Elbow Extensions
cues: Fully straighten the arm and turn the palm down
Then bend and turn the palm up

flexibility.name: Doorway Biceps Stretch
cues: Hold the doorframe at hip height, thumb down
Turn your body away until you feel the front of the arm stretch

name: Triceps
summary: The three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm — about two-thirds of your upper-arm size — that straightens the elbow.
functions: Pull the arm down and back (long head)
tips: Overhead extensions stretch the long head and are worth including.
Close-grip pressing lets you load the triceps heavily.

strength.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
cues: Hands about shoulder-width apart
Elbows tucked close to your sides
Touch the lower chest, press to lockout

strength.name: Cable Pushdown
cues: Elbows pinned to your sides
Push down until the arms are fully straight
Only the forearms move

strength.name: Overhead Dumbbell Extension
cues: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands
Lower it behind your head, elbows pointing up
Extend back up without flaring the elbows

strength.name: Bench Dips
cues: Hands on a bench behind you
Lower until the elbows reach about 90°
Keep your hips close to the bench

strength.name: Skull Crushers
cues: Lie on a bench, EZ bar over your forehead
Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward your head
Extend back up; keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling

strength.name: Diamond Push-ups
cues: Hands together under the chest, fingers forming a diamond
Lower with the elbows close to your body
Press back up to straight arms

flexibility.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
cues: Reach one arm overhead and bend the elbow
Use the other hand to ease the elbow back
Keep the ribs down

flexibility.name: Towel Behind-Back Stretch
cues: Hold a towel behind your back, one hand high, one low
Walk the hands toward each other

flexibility.name: Triceps Wall Stretch
cues: Elbow on a wall above your head, hand behind your neck
Lean gently into the wall

name: Forearms
summary: A group of muscles between the elbow and wrist that control your grip, wrist and finger movement.
tips: Grip strength often limits pulling exercises — direct grip work pays off.
Desk and phone work keeps the forearm flexors short; stretch them daily.

strength.name: Dead Hang
cues: Hang from a bar with a full grip
Keep the shoulders gently engaged
Breathe and hold

strength.name: Wrist Curls
cues: Forearms on your thighs, palms up
Curl the wrist up through its full range
Let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips at the bottom

strength.name: Reverse Curls
cues: Overhand grip, shoulder width
Curl with your wrists kept straight
Lower slowly

strength.name: Plate Pinch Hold
cues: Pinch two smooth plates together with your fingertips
Hold at your side without letting them slip

strength.name: Farmer's Carry
cues: Heavy dumbbells at your sides
Grip hard and walk tall
Short, controlled steps

strength.name: Wrist Roller
cues: Hold the roller at shoulder height, arms straight
Roll the weight up by twisting your wrists
Unroll it slowly back down

flexibility.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
cues: Arm straight ahead, palm up
Gently pull the fingers down and back

flexibility.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
cues: Arm straight ahead, palm down
Gently pull the back of the hand toward you

flexibility.name: Wrist Circles
cues: Interlace your fingers
Roll the wrists in smooth circles

flexibility.name: Prayer Stretch
cues: Palms together in front of your chest
Slowly lower the hands toward your waist, keeping the palms together

name: Abs
summary: The 'six-pack' muscle running down the front of the abdomen, plus the deep corset muscle beneath it that braces the spine.
functions: Flex the trunk (curl the ribs toward the pelvis)
Increase pressure in the abdomen when breathing out hard
tips: Visible abs depend mostly on body-fat level, not ab exercises.
Anti-extension work (planks, rollouts) builds a core that transfers to lifting.

strength.name: Plank
cues: Forearms under the shoulders
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the pelvis slightly
Don't let the hips sag

strength.name: Hanging Knee Raise
cues: Hang with straight arms
Curl the pelvis up and bring the knees toward the chest
Lower without swinging

strength.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Start kneeling, wheel under the shoulders
Roll out while keeping the lower back flat
Pull back with the abs, not the hips

strength.name: Cable Crunch
cues: Kneel facing the stack, rope by your head
Crunch the ribs toward the pelvis
Hips stay still

strength.name: Dead Bug
cues: Lie on your back, arms up, knees at 90°
Extend the opposite arm and leg slowly
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor

strength.name: Hollow Body Hold
cues: Lie on your back, arms overhead
Lift shoulders and legs, pressing the lower back down
Hold the banana shape and breathe

strength.name: Reverse Crunch
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent at 90°
Curl the hips off the floor toward your chest
Lower slowly without swinging

flexibility.name: Cobra Stretch
cues: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders
Press the chest up, keeping the hips down
Only go as high as is comfortable for the lower back

flexibility.name: Standing Side-to-Side Reach
cues: Reach both arms overhead
Lean gently to each side and slightly back

flexibility.name: Upward Dog
cues: From lying face down, press up with straight arms
Lift the thighs off the floor
Keep the shoulders away from the ears

flexibility.name: Standing Back Bend
cues: Hands on your lower back
Lift the chest and lean back gently
Return to standing

name: Obliques
summary: The muscles along the sides of the waist that twist and bend the trunk and resist rotation.
functions: Resist twisting and side-bending under load
tips: Anti-rotation exercises (Pallof press, suitcase carry) are especially useful for sport and back health.
The serratus anterior sits on the ribs and keeps the shoulder blades against the ribcage.

strength.name: Side Plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder
Body in one straight line from head to feet
Push the floor away and lift the hips

strength.name: Pallof Press
cues: Stand side-on to the cable, handle at your chest
Press straight out and resist being twisted
Hold for 2 s, return

strength.name: Cable Woodchop
cues: Pull diagonally from high to low across your body
Rotate through the torso, pivot the back foot
Arms stay mostly straight

strength.name: Suitcase Carry
cues: Heavy weight in one hand only
Stay perfectly upright — don't lean
Walk slowly

strength.name: Russian Twist
cues: Sit leaning back, feet up or on the floor
Rotate the weight from side to side
Turn through the ribs, not just the arms

strength.name: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise
cues: Hang from a bar
Raise the knees up and toward one side
Lower under control and alternate

flexibility.name: Standing Side Bend
cues: Reach one arm overhead
Lean to the opposite side
Keep the hips stacked over the feet

flexibility.name: Supine Spinal Twist
cues: Lie on your back and drop both knees to one side
Keep both shoulders on the floor
Breathe into the side of the ribs

flexibility.name: Seated Torso Rotations
cues: Sit tall, arms crossed
Rotate slowly from the mid-back

flexibility.name: Seated Side Reach
cues: Sit cross-legged
Reach one arm overhead and lean to the opposite side
Keep both sitting bones grounded

name: Lats
summary: The widest muscles of the back, running from the lower spine and pelvis up into the upper arm. They create the V-taper.
functions: Pull the arms down and toward the body
Help stabilise the spine during heavy lifts
tips: Think 'elbows to hips' to feel the lats during pulldowns and rows.
Tight lats can limit how far you can raise your arms overhead.

strength.name: Pull-ups
cues: Overhand grip, slightly wider than the shoulders
Pull the elbows down to your sides
Chin over the bar, lower to a full hang

strength.name: Lat Pulldown
cues: Lean back slightly, chest up
Pull the bar to your upper chest
Control it back to straight arms

strength.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
cues: One hand and knee on a bench, back flat
Row the dumbbell toward your hip
Let the shoulder blade stretch at the bottom

strength.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
cues: Arms straight, slight hinge at the hips
Sweep the bar down to your thighs
Keep the elbows locked softly

strength.name: Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip)
cues: Wide overhand grip on a long bar
Pull to the lower chest, elbows out
Control the stretch forward

strength.name: Dumbbell Pullover
cues: Lie across a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest
Lower it behind your head with slightly bent arms
Pull it back over the chest using the lats

strength.name: Inverted Row
cues: Hang under a bar set at waist height
Keep the body straight and pull your chest to the bar
Lower slowly

flexibility.name: Child's Pose with Side Reach
cues: Kneel and sit back toward your heels
Walk both hands over to one side
Breathe into the side of the ribs

flexibility.name: Overhead Lat Stretch
cues: Hold a post or doorframe at head height
Sink the hips back and away
Let the arm and side lengthen

flexibility.name: Bench Lat Stretch
cues: Kneel facing a bench, elbows on it, hands together
Sink the chest toward the floor
Keep the hips back over the knees

flexibility.name: Dead Hang Stretch
cues: Hang from a bar with relaxed shoulders
Let the body lengthen
Breathe slowly

name: Upper Back
summary: The muscles around and between the shoulder blades, including part of the rotator cuff. Key for posture and healthy shoulders.
functions: Rotate the upper arm outward (rotator cuff)
Hold the shoulder joint in place during movement
tips: Aim for at least as much pulling as pressing each week.
External-rotation work is cheap insurance for the shoulder.

strength.name: Chest-Supported Row
cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench
Row the dumbbells with the elbows out at ~45°
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top

strength.name: Seated Cable Row
cues: Sit tall, slight bend in the knees
Pull the handle to your stomach
Shoulders down, not shrugged

strength.name: Band External Rotation
cues: Elbow at your side, bent to 90°
Rotate the forearm outward against the band
Keep the elbow tucked in

strength.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
cues: Hinge to about 45° with a flat back
Row the bar to the lower ribs
No jerking with the hips

strength.name: Reverse Fly
cues: Hinge forward with a flat back
Raise light dumbbells out to the sides
Squeeze the shoulder blades together

strength.name: Prone T-Raises
cues: Lie face down, arms out to the sides
Lift the arms, thumbs up, squeezing the blades together
Lower slowly

flexibility.name: Thread the Needle
cues: Start on all fours
Slide one arm under your body, letting the shoulder drop
Then rotate and reach it to the ceiling

flexibility.name: Upper Back Hug Stretch
cues: Wrap your arms around yourself
Round the upper back and spread the shoulder blades
Breathe into the back of the ribs

flexibility.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
cues: Roller under the upper back, hands behind your head
Gently extend over it
Move the roller up a few centimetres and repeat

flexibility.name: Cross-Body Scapular Stretch
cues: Pull one arm across your chest
Round the upper back slightly
Feel the stretch between the shoulder blades

name: Lower Back
summary: The columns of muscle running up either side of the spine that keep you upright and protect the spine when you bend and lift.
functions: Extend the spine (stand up from bending)
Hold the spine neutral under load
tips: Train it to resist movement first (bird dogs, carries) before loading it heavily.
Persistent or sharp back pain should be checked by a professional before training through it.

strength.name: Bird Dog
cues: Start on all fours, spine neutral
Extend the opposite arm and leg
Don't let the hips rotate

strength.name: Back Extension
cues: Hips on the pad, ankles locked in
Lower with a flat back, hinging at the hips
Rise until the body is in a straight line — no over-arching

strength.name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Soft knees, push the hips back
Bar slides down the thighs
Keep the back flat; stand up by driving the hips forward

strength.name: Deadlift
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins close
Brace hard and pull the slack out of the bar
Push the floor away and lock out with the glutes

strength.name: Superman Hold
cues: Lie face down, arms overhead
Lift arms, chest and legs slightly
Keep the neck neutral and breathe

strength.name: Good Morning
cues: Light bar across the upper back
Hinge at the hips with soft knees
Return upright by driving the hips forward

flexibility.name: Cat–Cow
cues: On all fours
Alternate rounding and arching the spine
Move with your breath

flexibility.name: Knees-to-Chest
cues: Lie on your back
Hug both knees toward your chest
Let the lower back relax into the floor

flexibility.name: Child's Pose
cues: Kneel, sit back toward your heels
Reach the arms forward and rest your forehead down

flexibility.name: Supine Lumbar Rotation
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent together
Rock the knees side to side
Keep the shoulders on the floor

name: Glutes
summary: The largest and most powerful muscles in the body. They extend the hip for running, jumping and lifting, and stabilise the pelvis.
functions: Move the leg out to the side (glute medius)
Stabilise the pelvis when standing on one leg
tips: Weak glute medius often shows as knees caving in during squats.
Long periods of sitting can make the glutes switch off — activation drills help.

strength.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Upper back on a bench, bar over the hips
Drive through the heels to lift the hips
Chin tucked; squeeze hard at the top

strength.name: Glute Bridge
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent
Push through the heels and lift the hips
Don't arch the lower back

strength.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Rear foot up on a bench
Lean the torso slightly forward
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor

strength.name: Banded Lateral Walk
cues: Band around the knees or ankles
Half-squat position
Step sideways and keep tension on the band

strength.name: Cable Kickback
cues: Ankle strap on a low pulley
Kick the leg straight back
Squeeze the glute without arching the back

strength.name: Step-ups
cues: Step onto a box with your whole foot
Drive through the heel to stand up
Lower slowly on the same leg

flexibility.name: Figure-4 Stretch
cues: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Pull the bottom leg toward you
Keep the crossed knee opening outward

flexibility.name: Pigeon Pose
cues: Front shin across the mat, back leg straight behind
Keep the hips square
Fold forward for a deeper stretch

flexibility.name: Leg Swings (side to side)
cues: Hold a wall for balance
Swing the leg across your body and out to the side

flexibility.name: Seated Glute Stretch
cues: Sit tall and cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Hinge forward from the hips
Keep the back long

name: Adductors
summary: The inner-thigh muscles that pull the legs together and help stabilise the hips in squats and changes of direction.
functions: Pull the legs toward the midline
Stabilise the pelvis while walking and running
tips: Groin strains are common in sports with sprinting and cutting — the Copenhagen plank is a well-researched preventive exercise.
Wide-stance squats load the adductors heavily.

strength.name: Copenhagen Plank
cues: Side plank with your top leg resting on a bench
Lift the hips and the bottom leg off the floor
Start with the knee on the bench to make it easier

strength.name: Sumo Squat
cues: Wide stance, toes turned out
Hold a dumbbell between your legs
Push the knees out as you squat

strength.name: Hip Adduction Machine
cues: Pads on the inner knees
Squeeze the legs together slowly
Control the return

strength.name: Cossack Squat
cues: Very wide stance
Shift your weight to one side and squat deep on that leg
The other leg stays straight with toes up

strength.name: Side-Lying Adduction
cues: Lie on your side, top foot in front
Lift the bottom leg toward the ceiling
Lower slowly

strength.name: Cable Hip Adduction
cues: Ankle strap, stand side-on to the cable
Sweep the leg across in front of the other
Control the return

flexibility.name: Butterfly Stretch
cues: Sit with the soles of your feet together
Let the knees drop toward the floor
Hinge forward from the hips with a long spine

flexibility.name: Frog Stretch
cues: On all fours, slide the knees wide
Ankles in line with the knees
Rock the hips back gently

flexibility.name: Lateral Lunge Rocks
cues: Wide stance
Shift side to side, sitting into the bent leg

flexibility.name: Wide-Leg Forward Fold
cues: Stand with your feet wide
Hinge forward and let the hands reach the floor
Keep the knees soft

name: Quadriceps
summary: Four muscles at the front of the thigh that straighten the knee — essential for squatting, climbing stairs, jumping and running.
functions: Absorb force when landing and going downhill
tips: Letting the knees travel forward over the toes in a squat is normal and loads the quads more.
Strong quads support healthy knees.

strength.name: Back Squat
cues: Bar on the upper back, feet shoulder-width
Brace, then sit down between your hips
Knees track over the toes; stand up driving through the mid-foot

strength.name: Goblet Squat
cues: Hold a dumbbell against your chest
Squat deep with the elbows inside the knees
Chest stays up

strength.name: Leg Press
cues: Feet hip-width in the middle of the platform
Lower until the knees reach ~90° or deeper
Don't let the lower back lift off the pad

strength.name: Walking Lunges
cues: Take a long step forward
Drop the back knee toward the floor
Push through the front foot into the next step

strength.name: Leg Extension
cues: Knee lined up with the machine's pivot
Straighten fully and pause
Lower slowly

strength.name: Front Squat
cues: Bar resting on the front of the shoulders, elbows high
Sit straight down with an upright torso
Drive up through the mid-foot

strength.name: Split Squat
cues: Long stance, back heel up
Lower the back knee toward the floor
Push through the front foot

flexibility.name: Standing Quad Stretch
cues: Hold your ankle behind you
Keep the knees together
Tuck the pelvis to feel it at the front of the hip

flexibility.name: Couch Stretch
cues: Back knee on the floor against a wall, shin up the wall
Front foot forward in a lunge
Squeeze the glute and stay upright

flexibility.name: Walking Knee-to-Butt
cues: Walk forward, pulling the heel to your glute each step

flexibility.name: Side-Lying Quad Stretch
cues: Lie on your side and hold the top ankle
Pull the heel toward your glute
Push the hip forward slightly

name: Hamstrings
summary: Three muscles at the back of the thigh that bend the knee and extend the hip. They are frequently strained in sprinting.
functions: Extend the hip with the glutes
Slow the leg down during sprinting
tips: Train both jobs: hip hinges (RDLs) and knee flexion (curls).
Nordic curls are strongly linked to fewer hamstring strains in research on athletes.

strength.name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Soft knees, hips push straight back
Bar stays close to the legs
Stop when you feel a strong stretch, then drive the hips forward

strength.name: Lying Leg Curl
cues: Hips pressed into the pad
Curl the heels toward your glutes
Lower over 3 seconds

strength.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
cues: Kneel with your ankles anchored
Lower your body forward as slowly as possible
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up

strength.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell RDL
cues: Hinge on one leg as the other reaches back
Keep the hips level
Feel the stretch in the standing leg

strength.name: Seated Leg Curl
cues: Pad above the ankles, thighs locked in
Curl the heels down and back
Control the return

strength.name: Glute-Ham Raise
cues: Feet locked in, knees on the pad
Lower forward under control
Curl back up using the hamstrings

flexibility.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
cues: Heel on a low step, toes up
Hinge forward with a flat back
Keep a slight bend in the knee

flexibility.name: Supine Strap Stretch
cues: Lie on your back, strap around one foot
Raise the straight leg until you feel the stretch
Keep the other leg flat

flexibility.name: Leg Swings (front to back)
cues: Hold a wall for balance
Swing the leg forward and back, gradually higher

flexibility.name: Seated Forward Fold
cues: Sit with your legs straight
Hinge forward from the hips
Reach toward your feet without forcing it

name: Calves
summary: The muscles at the back of the lower leg that point the foot and propel you when walking, running and jumping.
tips: Straight-knee raises target the gastrocnemius; bent-knee raises target the soleus.
Calves respond well to a full range of motion and slow negatives.

strength.name: Standing Calf Raise
cues: Balls of the feet on the edge of a step
Drop the heels into a deep stretch
Rise as high as you can and pause

strength.name: Seated Calf Raise
cues: Knees bent at 90° under the pad
Full range: stretch to peak contraction

strength.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
cues: Stand on one foot on a step
Hold a wall lightly for balance
Slow, full reps

strength.name: Jump Rope
cues: Stay on the balls of your feet
Small, quick bounces

strength.name: Donkey Calf Raise
cues: Hinge forward at the hips, balls of the feet on a step
Lower the heels deep
Rise as high as possible

strength.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
cues: Balls of the feet on the bottom edge of the platform
Push through the toes
Full stretch on every rep

flexibility.name: Wall Calf Stretch
cues: Hands on a wall, one leg back with a straight knee
Press the back heel into the floor
Bend that knee slightly to shift the stretch to the soleus

flexibility.name: Downward Dog Pedal
cues: In a downward dog position
Alternately press each heel toward the floor

flexibility.name: Soleus Wall Stretch
cues: Same as the wall calf stretch, but bend the back knee
Keep the heel down

flexibility.name: Step Heel Drop
cues: Stand on the edge of a step
Let one heel sink below the step
Hold a rail for balance

name: Shins
summary: The muscle along the front of the shin that lifts the toes and controls the foot as it lands.
functions: Control the foot coming down when walking
tips: Often overlooked, but strengthening it can help with shin splints and knee-over-toe positions.
Tibialis raises need no equipment beyond a wall.

strength.name: Tibialis Wall Raise
cues: Lean your back against a wall, heels about 30 cm out
Lift the toes as high as possible
Lower slowly

strength.name: Heel Walks
cues: Walk on your heels with the toes pulled up
Stand tall

strength.name: Banded Dorsiflexion
cues: Sit with your leg straight, band around the top of the foot and anchored ahead
Pull the toes back toward you

strength.name: Toe Raises (Seated)
cues: Sit with your feet flat
Lift your toes as high as possible, heels down
Lower slowly

strength.name: Tibialis Raise (Weighted)
cues: Sit on a bench with a light plate on top of your feet
Lift the toes against the weight
Lower slowly

flexibility.name: Kneeling Shin Stretch
cues: Kneel with the tops of your feet flat on the floor
Sit back gently toward your heels

flexibility.name: Ankle Circles
cues: Lift one foot
Draw slow, large circles with your toes

flexibility.name: Standing Shin Stretch
cues: Point the toes behind you, resting the top of the foot on the floor
Gently push the ankle toward the floor
